pull_request.title: fix: resolve manifest generation issues, update oclif tooling
pull_request.body:
<!-- Describe your Pull Request -->

This PR resovles manifest generation issues. Specifically, it reverts two changes that were made to remove using `delete` with variables, assigning them to `undefined` instead. I've also updated biome to `warn` rather than `error` on these instances - we do want to change the instances of `delete` eventually, but it's fine to keep them in for now. I've also run the readme update tool that oclif provides, which has implemented a number of changes.

Additionally, I've updated `oclif` tooling to use the versions supported by oclif now and have added npm scripts so we don't have to remember which commands we need to run.

issue.title: Request: Omitting experimental flags from new config file
issue.body:
Opening this issue on behalf of several individuals with whom I spoke about the new configuration file landed in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/57016 ...

The specific request from three separate people in separate conversations is to specifically omit `--experimental-*` flags from the configuration file format, even if hose flags are otherwise allowed in `NODE_OPTIONS`.

/cc @marco-ippolito @ljharb @ShogunPanda @anonrig @joyeecheung @mhdawson @bnb (as the folks who authored/reviewed that PR)

comment.body:
I'm generally +1 to @joyeecheung's suggestions as general enhancements, regardless of which direction we go with this discussion.

> What about denylist some of the experimental feature we don't want to support in the config file?

I'm concerned about this because then you have to know which ones work and which don't and it could be very confusing for developers. IMO being consistent with how things are applied _broadly_ in a config file is super important for good DX.

I'd like to propose something totally different:

We _could_ build-in a feature that can maintain flags for you, as the project prefers. Did Node.js v32.0.0 promote the `experimental-jsonc-support` feature to stable? Run something like `node --upgrade-noderc` or `node --upgrade-noderc --only=experimental-features` and we can automatically sort it out for you.

This could enable a few things:

- Potential for more rapid adoption of the `.noderc` file because we're doing good work that's annoying to do currently 
- The project can have more direct input with our users on how flags are used, providing a path for users to rely on our defaults
- Bring upgrades both of Node.js itself and of features we're shipping more to the forefront for developers
- This one's a bit more half-baked, but I think it _could_ serve as an escape hatch for maintainers both who *do* want to support experimental features and who *don't* as it upstreams the problem of maintaining those features to us
